segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Jesus told a story about the smallest seed a farmer knew.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It was a mustard seed — so tiny it could be lost in the palm of your hand.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: A man took that one little seed and planted it in his field.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Of all the seeds he could have sown, it was just about the smallest of them all.

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: which indeed is the least of all seeds:

segments.speaker: jesus
segments.text: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But that tiny seed did not stay small. Quietly, slowly, it began to grow.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Up out of the ground, higher and higher, until it became the largest plant in the whole garden — a tall, spreading tree.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And the wild birds came and built their nests in its broad, sheltering branches.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: That, Jesus said, is what God's kingdom is like.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: It almost never begins big. It begins small — a whispered prayer, a single kind act, one quiet change of heart.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But God takes that smallest beginning and grows it into something far greater than anyone could have imagined.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: God does enormous things from the smallest of starts. What small seed is he asking you to plant today?
